questions.q: What is the name of the Structured Streaming source that Auto Loader provides?

options.t: autoLoaderSource

options.t: cloudFiles
deltaFiles
options.why: The source format is cloudFiles.

options.t: fileStream

questions.q: Where does Auto Loader keep track of the files it has already processed?

options.t: In RocksDB inside the stream's checkpoint location
In a Delta table named _auto_loader_files in the target schema
options.why: Discovered files are tracked in RocksDB inside the checkpoint location.

options.t: In the source folder, by renaming each file after it is read
options.why: Auto Loader doesn't rename or move source files; it tracks them in the checkpoint.

options.t: In the Unity Catalog metastore, as a property of the volume
options.why: File tracking lives in the checkpoint, not in catalog metadata.

questions.explain: Auto Loader keeps the metadata of discovered files in RocksDB in the checkpoint location, which gives exactly-once processing and lets a failed stream resume where it stopped.

questions.q: An Auto Loader stream's checkpoint folder is deleted by mistake, and the stream is started again with the same checkpoint path. What happens?

options.t: It continues exactly where it stopped, because the target table remembers the files
options.why: Progress lives in the checkpoint; without it, the stream starts fresh.

options.t: It fails until the old checkpoint is restored from backup
options.why: It doesn't fail; a missing checkpoint just means a fresh start.

options.t: It starts fresh and processes the source files again from the beginning
It processes only files that arrive after the restart
options.why: A fresh start includes existing files unless told otherwise, so earlier files are read again.

questions.explain: The checkpoint holds Auto Loader's file tracking and the query's offsets and commits; deleting it (or pointing to a new one) makes the next run start fresh, reprocessing the source.

questions.q: Which file detection mode does Auto Loader use by default?

options.t: File notification with cloud queues
options.why: File notification is optional; directory listing is the default.

options.t: File events from Unity Catalog, always
options.why: File events are recommended with file notification, but the default mode is directory listing.

options.t: Polling the target table for new partitions
options.why: Auto Loader looks at the source location, not the target table.

options.t: Directory listing

questions.explain: Directory listing is the default and needs only read access to the data; file notification uses cloud notification and queue services.

questions.q: For most workloads, which file detection setup does Databricks recommend for Auto Loader?

options.t: File notification with Unity Catalog file events enabled on the external location
Directory listing with a very short trigger interval
options.why: Databricks recommends file notification with file events for most workloads.

options.t: File notification with a storage queue that you create, permission and manage yourself
options.why: With file events on the external location, no extra setup or permissions are needed.

options.t: Listing the source folder in a separate job and passing names to Auto Loader
options.why: Auto Loader discovers files itself; the recommendation is file notification with file events.

questions.explain: Databricks recommends file notification with file events for most workloads; with file events on the external location, no extra permissions are needed.

questions.q: A downstream step assumes Auto Loader processes files in the order they arrived. Which statement is correct?

options.t: Order is guaranteed in directory listing mode only
options.why: Auto Loader never guarantees file order, in either mode.

options.t: Order is guaranteed in file notification mode only
options.why: Auto Loader never guarantees file order, in either mode.

options.t: Auto Loader never guarantees file order, in either mode
Order is guaranteed whenever maxFilesPerTrigger is set to 1
options.why: The documentation states no ordering guarantee in either mode.

questions.explain: Auto Loader never guarantees the order in which files are processed; logic must not depend on file order.

questions.q: Auto Loader infers the schema of JSON files without any type options. What types do the inferred columns get?

options.t: The narrowest type that fits the sampled values
options.why: For JSON, CSV and XML, columns are inferred as string unless inferColumnTypes is true.

options.t: STRING, unless cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes is true
VARIANT for every column
options.why: Without inferColumnTypes, JSON columns are inferred as string.

options.t: Types read from a schema stored inside each JSON file
options.why: JSON carries no schema; Parquet and Avro bring their own types.

questions.explain: For JSON, CSV and XML every column is inferred as string unless cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes is true; Parquet and Avro use their own types.

questions.q: Where does Auto Loader store the schema it infers?

options.t: In a _schemas folder under cloudFiles.schemaLocation
In the target table's properties only
options.why: Auto Loader keeps its inferred schema in a _schemas folder at the schema location.

options.t: Nowhere: it re-infers the schema on every micro-batch
options.why: The schema is stored, so it isn't re-inferred from scratch each time.

options.t: In the source folder, as a schema.json file next to the data
options.why: It writes to the schema location, not the source folder.

questions.explain: Set cloudFiles.schemaLocation (it can be the checkpoint path); the inferred schema is stored in a _schemas directory there.

questions.q: How much data does Auto Loader sample for its first schema inference?

options.t: Every file in the source folder
options.why: It samples a bounded amount: the first 50 GB or 1,000 files.

options.t: Only the first file
options.why: It samples up to 50 GB or 1,000 files.

options.t: The first 100 MB, whatever the file count
options.why: The documented limits are 50 GB or 1,000 files.

options.t: The first 50 GB or 1,000 files

questions.explain: The first inference samples the first 50 GB or 1,000 files.

questions.q: Auto Loader infers `amount` as STRING, but it must be DECIMAL(10,2). Without giving a full schema, how do you set that one column's type?

options.t: cast(amount AS DECIMAL(10,2)) in a separate silver job only
options.why: Possible downstream, but Auto Loader itself lets you override inferred types with schema hints.

options.t: cloudFiles.schemaHints, for example "amount DECIMAL(10,2)"
cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode = rescue
options.why: That controls what happens with new columns, not the type of an existing one.

options.t: mergeSchema = true on the write
options.why: mergeSchema evolves the target schema; it doesn't set an inferred column's type.

questions.explain: Schema hints (cloudFiles.schemaHints) override inferred types for chosen columns.

questions.q: When Auto Loader infers a schema, it adds a `_rescued_data` column. What goes into it?

options.t: Rows that failed a data quality expectation
options.why: Expectations are a pipeline feature; _rescued_data holds values that don't fit the schema.

options.t: Copies of rows that a later MERGE or DELETE removed from the target table, kept for audit
options.why: It holds values from incoming files that don't fit the schema.

options.t: Values that don't fit the schema: wrong types, unexpected columns, different case
The names of files that couldn't be read
options.why: It holds data values, not file names.

questions.explain: The rescued data column collects values that don't fit the schema (a wrong type, an unexpected column, a different case) instead of losing them.

questions.q: With the default schema evolution mode and no schema given, new files bring a column `city`. What happens?

options.t: The stream adds the column to the table silently and carries on, with no failure or restart
options.why: addNewColumns fails the stream first, then resumes with the new column on restart.

options.t: The stream fails with an unknown-field error, and resumes with `city` on restart
The new column is ignored and its values are lost
options.why: That is mode none, which is the default only when you give a schema.

options.t: The new values go to _rescued_data and the schema never changes
options.why: That is rescue mode, not the default.

questions.explain: addNewColumns is the default without a given schema: the stream fails with UnknownFieldException after recording the new column, and resumes with the new schema on restart.

questions.q: Because the default Auto Loader evolution mode fails the stream on a new column, how does Databricks recommend running such streams?

options.t: As Lakeflow Jobs that restart automatically on failure, or in pipelines
On an all-purpose cluster that someone watches during business hours
options.why: Production streams should restart automatically; all-purpose compute isn't for production jobs.

options.t: With schema evolution disabled entirely, so that the stream can never fail on a new column
options.why: The recommendation is automatic restart, so evolution works as designed.

options.t: With a new checkpoint for every run
options.why: A new checkpoint reprocesses everything; a restart with the same checkpoint picks up the new schema.

questions.explain: Databricks recommends running Auto Loader streams as Lakeflow Jobs that restart automatically, since addNewColumns deliberately fails and then succeeds on restart.

questions.q: Which Auto Loader schema evolution mode never evolves the schema and never fails, sending new columns to `_rescued_data`?

options.t: addNewColumns
options.why: addNewColumns evolves the schema, failing once first.

options.t: failOnNewColumns
options.why: failOnNewColumns fails until the schema or file is fixed.

options.t: none

options.t: rescue

questions.explain: rescue never evolves or fails; new columns go to the rescued data column.

questions.q: You give Auto Loader an explicit schema and set no evolution mode. Files then arrive with an extra column. What happens to it?

options.t: The stream fails with an unknown-field error
options.why: With a schema given, the default mode is none, which doesn't fail.

options.t: It is ignored, and not rescued unless rescuedDataColumn is set
It is added to the table automatically
options.why: none never evolves the schema.

options.t: It goes into _rescued_data automatically
options.why: With mode none, new columns aren't rescued unless rescuedDataColumn is set.

questions.explain: When you give a schema, the default mode is none: new columns are ignored and not rescued unless the rescuedDataColumn option is set.

addNewColumns

A separate target table per folder; one table can't take two streams

questions.q: An Auto Loader stream in file notification mode fails with CLOUD_FILE_SOURCE_FILE_NOT_FOUND. What is the likely cause?

options.t: The checkpoint was shared with another stream
options.why: That causes a concurrent transaction error on a Delta sink, not this one.

options.t: The file's schema didn't match the inferred schema
options.why: Schema mismatches go to rescued data or trigger evolution, not this error.

options.t: The storage account's firewall blocked serverless compute
options.why: That shows as 403 Forbidden, not a missing notified file.

questions.explain: CLOUD_FILE_SOURCE_FILE_NOT_FOUND says a file notification was received for a file that no longer exists: files must not be deleted before they are processed.

questions.q: Which statements about Auto Loader are true?

options.t: It gives exactly-once processing of discovered files
It can include files that already exist when it starts
It guarantees files are processed in arrival order
options.why: Auto Loader never guarantees file order.

options.t: It reads only Parquet files
options.why: It reads JSON, CSV, XML, Parquet, Avro, ORC, text and binary files.

options.t: It needs a Lakeflow Connect connection to run
options.why: Auto Loader is a Structured Streaming source; it needs no connection object.

questions.explain: Auto Loader processes new files exactly once, tracked in RocksDB in the checkpoint, and can include existing files; it reads many formats and never guarantees order.

The output mode, set to update
